newsitem.title: USA: First Bank charge-offs rise in Q1.
newsitem.headline: First Bank charge-offs rise in Q1.

text.p: First Bank Systems Inc on Wednesday said its net loan charge-offs and provision for credit losses rose in the first quarter because of increased loan volumes and higher consumer net charge-offs.

Total annualized net charge-offs were 0.62 percent of average loans in the first quarter, compared to 0.51 percent in the year-earlier quarter and 0.59 percent in the fourth quarter, the bank holding company said.
Annualized credit card net charge-offs were 3.86 percent in the first quarter, compared to 3.01 percent in the 1906 quarter and 3.57 percent in the fourth quarter, First Bank said.
Analysts have said consumer loan charge-offs throughout the banking sector have been reaching a level that merited concern.
The ratio of credit loss allowances to non-performing assets continued to indicate strong reserve coverage at 381 percent, compared with 337 percent at March 31, 1996, the company said.

First Bank, which last month announced it was merging with U.S. Bancorp, said net operating income rose to $171.8 million, or $1.27 a share, in the first quarter from $160.1 million, or $1.14, in the year-earlier period.
The mean analyst estimate was $1.26 a share, according to First Call.
Shares of First Bank, which has $36 billion in assets, were 3/8 higher at 74-3/4 early Wednesday afternoon.
